html:
Marduk was the god of the city of Babylon in ancient Mesopotamia, who rose with its power to become king of the gods. His temple, the Esagila, stood at the city's heart beside the great ziggurat.

At first he was a minor god. When Hammurabi made Babylon master of Mesopotamia in the 1700s BCE, in the Old Babylonian kingdom, Marduk rose too. The epic Enuma Elish tells how he killed the sea monster Tiamat, made heaven and earth from her body, and was made king of the gods. It was recited at the New Year festival, when the king of Babylonia took the god's hand to renew his right to rule.

Conquerors carried off his statue more than once, and its return marked Babylon's revival. Under Nebuchadnezzar II his beast, the snake-dragon, decorated the Ishtar Gate. When Cyrus took Babylon in 539 BCE, the Cyrus Cylinder claimed that Marduk himself had chosen Cyrus to replace the impious king Nabonidus. His worship faded under Persian and Greek rule. The Bible calls him Merodach.
sum: Marduk was the god of the city of Babylon in ancient Mesopotamia, who rose with its power to become king of the gods. His temple, the Esagila, stood at the city's heart beside the great ziggurat.
